chunks: 5192 - Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"The privacy of the believer is forbidden to another believer."

And he said: "Whoever spies upon a believer in his home, then his two eyes are lawful to the believer in that situation. And whoever storms upon a believer in his home without his permission, then his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation. And whoever denies the prophethood of a sent prophet and rejects him, then his blood is lawful."

He said: So I said to him, "What is the condition of one who rejects the Imam from among you?" He said: "Whoever rejects an Imam has dissociated himself from Allah, and He is dissociated from him and from his religion. So he is a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, because the Imam is from Allah and his religion is the religion of Allah. And whoever dissociates himself from the religion of Allah, then he is a disbeliever, and his blood is lawful in that situation, unless he returns and repents to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, from what he said."
He said: "And whoever assaults a believer, intending his wealth and his life, then his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation."

key_terms.دَمُهُ مُبَاحٌ: his blood is deemed licit in that legal situation
key_terms.عَوْرَةُ الْمُؤْمِنِ: the protected privacy and inviolable personal sanctity of the believer
key_terms.يَتُوبَ إِلَى اللَّهِ: to repent and return to Allah

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about violating a believer’s privacy and rejecting the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sanctity of a believer’s privacy, life, and protected status, and it discusses legal consequences for spying, unlawful intrusion, violent assault, and rejection of divinely appointed religious authority. It also presents a strong doctrinal statement on the status of one who denies a prophet or an Imam and mentions repentance as the path of return.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5192 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:
"The privacy (awrah) of a believer is forbidden upon another believer."

Imam (as) also said: "Whoever spies on a believer in his home, his eyes are lawful to the believer in that situation. Whoever forcefully enters upon a believer in his home without his permission, his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation. And whoever denies the Prophethood of a divinely sent prophet and rejects him, his blood is lawful."

I then asked Imam (as): "What about someone who rejects the Imam from among you (Ahlulbayt (as)) - what is his status?"
Imam (as) replied: "Whoever rejects an Imam has disassociated from Allah (swt), and Allah (swt) has disassociated from him, as well as from his religion. He is a disbeliever, an apostate from Islam, because the Imam is appointed by Allah (swt), and his religion is the religion of Allah (swt).
Whoever disassociates from the religion of Allah (swt) is a disbeliever, and his blood is lawful in that situation unless he repents and returns to Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, from what he has said."
Imam (as) further said: "Whoever attacks a believer intending to harm his wealth or his life, his blood is lawful to the believer in that situation."
